parts.label: General radial electric field
parts.help: For the strictly infinite half-planes there is no finite general cutoff-independent field. Review the logarithmic divergence and finite-L regularization in the solution. Do not invent a finite value.

parts.label: General tangential electric field
parts.help: The general-point component depends on the distant-boundary regularization. Review the finite-L field and its projection. Cancellation is special to symmetry, not a general finite field.

parts.label: Radial field at S, α = 60°
parts.help: Even at S the radial field diverges logarithmically as a common cutoff L goes to infinity. A finite radius-independent field would be a false answer.

parts.label: Symmetric-cutoff tangential field at S
parts.help: Reflection symmetry makes this component exactly zero for every common finite cutoff. This does not make the full infinite-sheet field finite.

parts.label: Whether small displacements oscillate
parts.help: A finite cutoff and a taut string must first be specified. The regularized stability condition is QK_L < 0. The strictly infinite geometry is ill-posed.

parts.label: Oscillation frequency
parts.help: There is no finite cutoff-independent frequency. Review the regularized ω² = −QK_L/(mr). Never substitute a fabricated finite infinite-limit answer.
